analysis:
Scope: three BASE-side units of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 1000-2053): text submit via the v2 bridge, the cluster GLM/Qwen/MiMo media prepare paths, makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream, makeEventStream, tokenizer helpers. The patch excerpt is truncated and the changed head ranges (789-799, 821-824, 1044-1046, 1428-1430) are not shown in the supplied units. The excerpt shows the media path computing a reasoningPrefix from the rendered prompt before submitTokenized, and passing stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope) into the submit call. This is a parser-state and stop-string scoping change, not a change to authorization, attestation, encryption or the cache.

Security-relevant observations from the visible base code, none of them a regression. Cache isolation: cacheScope still flows into submitTokenized as the cache salt (T-041), and cluster media paths pass cacheEnabled false, which narrows the at-rest surface. Qwen media uses a lifetime/defer release (host.lifetime.releaseIfUnsubmitted), and the error paths call bridge.cancel and releaseBox.fire, so there are no obvious leaked pins or stalled GPU resources (T-010, T-029). Deadline checks wrap the stream construction. No plaintext prompt or output logging appears in the visible code; telemetry carries only operation and reason strings.

Open integration questions: (1) whether the new stopStringScope handling can suppress or leak stop sequences inside reasoning spans; this is a correctness question with no direct confidentiality impact visible. (2) The head hunks at lines 1044-1046 and 1428-1430 add one or more parameters, but the diff content is not visible. The BASE view of the submit calls shows no stopStringScope on the text path. Reviewers with the full patch should confirm that the new parameter is consistently threaded and that no cache or release behavior changed. No threat-model update is indicated from the supplied evidence.
